evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study.

claim: Future studies will be required to elucidate exactly how the intermediate state VSD is coupled to the pore to promote the IO conductance state.
source: and that future studies will be required to elucidate exactly how it is coupled to the pore to promote the IO conductance state.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The intermediate state VSD structure can be used in conjunction with the cryo-EM structure of KCNQ1 and with available models for both resting and fully activated human KCNQ1 to illuminate KCNQ1 pharmacology, physiology, and how some of the dozens of known LQTS disease mutations located in the VSD result in channel loss of function or dysfunction.
source: Even with the limitation indicated immediately above, the intermediate state VSD structure can be used in conjunction with the cryo-EM structure of KCNQ1 (Sun and MacKinnon, 2017) and with available models for both resting and fully activated human KCNQ1 (Kuenze et al., 2019) to illuminate KCNQ1 pharmacology, physiology, and how some of the dozens of known LQTS disease mutations located in the VSD result in channel loss of function or dysfunction (Tobelaim et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2018; Vanoye et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the structure.

claim: The KCNQ1 VSD intermediate state structure can be used as a template to model the intermediate state voltage sensors of other voltage-gated channels.
source: Moreover, the KCNQ1 VSD intermediate state structure can be used as a template to model the intermediate state voltage sensors of other voltage-gated channels, such as the Shaker potassium channel (Bezanilla et al., 1994; Zagotta et al., 1994; Baker et al., 1998; Jensen et al., 2012; Lacroix et al., 2012), and voltage-gated Na channels (DeCaen et al., 2008), which are believed to activate in a step-wise manner with S4 gating charges sequentially pairing with the charge transfer center and other acidic residues.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the structure with citations.

claim: This work utilizes KCNQ1's unique intermediate conductance to provide functional electrophysiology evidence that the VSD structure presented here truly represents the intermediate state conformation.
source: This work utilizes KCNQ1's unique intermediate conductance to provide functional electrophysiology evidence that the VSD structure presented here truly represents the intermediate state conformation.
evidence: This is a statement about the approach used for functional validation.

claim: Functional validation was based on two independent metrics, auxiliary subunit KCNE1 regulation and XE991 pharmacology.
source: We presented functional validation based on two independent metrics, auxiliary subunit KCNE1 regulation and XE991 pharmacology (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental approach.

claim: The fact that KCNE1 co-expression unambiguously discriminates channel mutants designed to stabilize the NMR VSD structure vs. the cryo-EM VSD structure constitutes compelling evidence that the two structures represent distinct functional KCNQ1 VSD states.
source: While the precise mechanism by which KCNE1 suppresses the IO state and enhances the AO state remains unclear, the fact that KCNE1 co-expression unambiguously discriminates channel mutants designed to stabilize the NMR VSD structure vs. the cryo-EM VSD structure constitutes compelling evidence that the two structures represent distinct functional KCNQ1 VSD states.
evidence: This is a statement about the strength of the evidence.

claim: Pharmacological studies of the same mutants by XE991 fully corroborate KCNE1 co-expression results.
source: Moreover, pharmacological studies of the same mutants by XE991 fully corroborate KCNE1 co-expression results
evidence: This is a statement about the consistency of the results.

claim: The functional validation data are robust and not dependent on any single functional result.
source: indicating that our functional validation data are robust and not dependent on any single functional result.

claim: Use of functional measurements to illuminate the properties of the intermediate state versus those of the activated state would be very challenging for KV channels that do populate an intermediate VSD state, but for which the pore is thought to only conduct current when its VSDs occupy the activated state.
source: By contrast, use of functional measurements to illuminate the properties of the intermediate state versus those of the activated state would be very challenging for KV channels that do populate an intermediate VSD state, but for which the pore is thought to only conduct current when its VSDs occupy the activated state, such as the Shaker channel.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges of studying other channels.

claim: In the case of the Shaker channel, functional electrophysiology would be unable to distinguish the intermediate state vs. the resting state of the VSD, as both states yield no ionic currents.
source: In the case of the Shaker channel, functional electrophysiology would be unable to distinguish the intermediate state vs. the resting state of the VSD, as both states yield no ionic currents.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of studying the Shaker channel.

claim: KCNQ1 represents a particularly suitable platform for structure-function study of the intermediate state in KV VSDs.
source: KCNQ1 thus represents a particularly suitable platform for structure-function study of the intermediate state in KV VSDs.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of studying KCNQ1.

claim: This work suggests a possible physiological role for the KCNQ1 intermediate conductance.
source: In addition to utilizing KCNQ1's intermediate conductance as a functional probe, this work also suggests a possible physiological role for the KCNQ1 intermediate conductance.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the work.

claim: Under physiological conditions where KCNQ1 is paired with KCNE3 as an accessory subunit, the channel is maximally conductive over a wide range of transmembrane voltages.
source: We demonstrated that under physiological conditions where KCNQ1 is paired with KCNE3 as an accessory subunit, the channel is maximally conductive over a wide range of transmembrane voltages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Depending on the transmembrane electrical potential, conductance may be a mix of the IO and AO states.
source: Depending on the transmembrane electrical potential, conductance may be a mix of the IO and AO states, as we observe that KCNE3 preserves both open states (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Two cryo-EM structures of the full-length KCNQ1/KCNE3/calmodulin complex with and without PIP2 were published during the revision of this manuscript.
source: Two cryo-EM structures of the full-length KCNQ1/KCNE3/calmodulin complex with and without PIP2 were published during the revision of this manuscript (Sun and MacKinnon, 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about recent publications.

source: In both new structures, the VSDs adopt the fully activated conformation at 0 mV membrane potential (Sun and MacKinnon, 2020)
evidence: This is a statement about the structures from a cited study.

claim: The primary function of the KCNQ1/KCNE3 complex is to serve as a leak channel in epithelial cells.
source: The primary function of the KCNQ1/KCNE3 complex is to serve as a leak channel in epithelial cells (Abbott, 2016; Julio-Kalajzić et al., 2018; Schroeder et al., 2000; Kroncke et al., 2016; Preston et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epithelial cells are non-excitable cells and not physiologically subject to the highly depolarizing membrane potentials required to activate substantial AO state conductance.
source: As epithelial cells are non-excitable cells and not physiologically subject to the highly depolarizing membrane potentials required to activate substantial AO state conductance
evidence: This is established knowledge about epithelial cell physiology.

claim: The IO state conductance likely constitutes the bulk of the physiological KCNQ1/KCNE3 leak K+ current in epithelial cells.
source: the IO state conductance likely constitutes the bulk of the physiological KCNQ1/KCNE3 leak K+ current in epithelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the understanding of epithelial cell physiology and the experimental data.

claim: The IO state is not merely a transient state on the pathway from resting to the AO state, but is itself an essential conductive state under some physiological conditions.
source: Thus, the IO state is not merely a transient state on the pathway from resting to the AO state. Rather, the data suggests that IO is itself an essential conductive state under some physiological conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: KCNE1 and KCNE3 promote different open states to confer exceptional functional versatility, uniquely tailoring KCNQ1 so that it can satisfy distinct physiological needs in different cell types and tissues.
